gaps.gap: No second host, no EKS/S3 in this container: the replays ran on the same container and CPU class as the producer (L0, 4 shared cores). Counted cost does not depend on the host, so the replays are valid; the wall-time columns (ns/GAE, end-to-end wall) are not independently reproduced.

Every replay used target/release/ecbench (sha256 b4fcf0ecdb3d0a0f42842856fe1e258258d52414c3ea54155292ae5431a592a0), the binary that produced the sessions. No cargo build was allowed, so there is no from-source rebuild as in research/ic_tableb_binary_ksum_20261115/validator. The independent checks are (a) a re-execution of all 480 deterministic runs per session by a different session than the producer's, (b) the validator's own Python prime-field arithmetic ([recovered]G == target for every record), and (c) an own recompute of every headline from records.jsonl.

No pcc claim filed and no keyring signature on the certificate or the report: every statement here is [pcc:unverified]. AGENTS.md 'Sabotage is assumed' asks for signed artifacts; none could be produced in this container.
bitop/v1 ratios are recomputed from each record's own work.bitops_per_sqrt_r field; the per-primitive bitop widths behind that field were not re-derived (the unit's definition is the producer's).
L0 runs, no isolation tier and no native L2/replay/A/A admission: valid for counted cost only; no wall-time or L2 claim is validated.

independent_of_producer: replay run by the validator session, after publication, with fresh invocations
own Python curve arithmetic for every scalar
own recompute of every headline (recompute.py), written without reading plot.py, summary.json, compare-*.txt or the README tables
not_independent: same container and CPU class (counted cost is host independent)

method: ecbench verify --replay-all --out <receipt> on each committed session (no copies; the session files were not modified), 3 sessions, every measured deterministic run re-executed and compared with its record (480 candidate runs per session), every recorded scalar checked by ecbench against its target; then, independently of ecbench, every record's [recovered]G == target re-checked with the validator's own Python affine arithmetic on the prime curve (generator order r checked, target on the curve).

scalar_certificates.method: own affine prime-field double-and-add: [recovered]G == target, target on y^2 = x^3 + ax + b, [r]G = O with r prime
